claims.claim: SolarEdge's Q2 2026 10-Q identifies accelerated U.S. clean-energy tax-credit phase-outs and elimination of the 25D homeowner credit as risks to customer economics, demand, competitiveness and revenue.
The filing states copper, lithium, nickel and cobalt price volatility is unhedged and can pressure margins when cost increases cannot be recovered from customers.

causalEdges.mechanism: weaker incentives can reduce customer returns and alter project timing
unhedged input inflation compresses margin when pricing cannot fully pass through costs

risks: Recovery durability remains exposed to policy-driven customer economics.
Unhedged commodity volatility can weaken operating leverage during a turnaround.
unknowns: Current evidence does not quantify the net demand elasticity to the revised U.S. tax-credit schedule or SolarEdge's realized pass-through capacity by product.

gatingStatus.note: Source-addressed risk support only; Alpha retains numeric underwriting authority.

recommendedNextStateOwner.action: Use the primary-source policy and commodity exposures in risk evidence and quantify only from Alpha-owned methodology inputs.
